turns.doctor_question: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
turns.patient_response: Hi. Well, I came in because I've had to be a lot more in front of people at work lately—I help plan events and meetings—and... I just can't stop staring at this one uneven-looking part of my face in photos. It really bothers me. Everyone else tells me they barely see anything, but I just can't seem to stop focusing on it.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient describes an inability to stop focusing on a perceived unevenness of their face that others report barely noticing, indicating preoccupation with a perceived defect in appearance.

turns.doctor_question: How certain are you that other people can clearly notice this unevenness in your face?
turns.patient_response: I mean... I don't know for sure. Like I said, people tell me they barely see it, or that I'm just being too hard on myself. But when I look in the mirror or see a picture, it just seems so obvious to me. So, I guess I'm not totally certain they see it the way I do, but it definitely feels like they must be noticing it when they look at me.

turns.doctor_question: When you become focused on this part of your face, do you repeatedly check it in mirrors or photos, compare it with others, or try to hide it?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I do. Especially at work. Before I send out event pictures or join a meeting with vendors, I'll keep checking my face in my phone camera. I end up retaking photos a lot, or I'll try to tilt my head a certain way so it doesn't look as bad. Sometimes I even ask a coworker if I look weird. It actually eats up enough time that I end up falling behind on my planning stuff.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient explicitly describes engaging in repetitive behaviors in response to appearance concerns, including repeatedly checking their face in the camera, retaking photos, tilting their head to conceal it, and seeking reassurance from coworkers.

turns.doctor_question: When your appearance is not a focus—for example, during a phone call—do you still fear being judged or embarrassed by other people?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. If I'm just on a phone call and they can't see me, I don't worry about it. It's really just when people are looking at my face or when I know there's a chance they might see a picture of me. If I'm just talking to someone on the phone, I feel fine.

turns.doctor_question: Do you recognize that your concern about this facial unevenness might be exaggerated, or are you completely convinced that it is clearly noticeable to others?
turns.patient_response: I guess I know it might be exaggerated. Like I mentioned before, people tell me they don't really see it, so part of me realizes it might just be in my head or at least not as bad as I think. But it's hard to shake the feeling when I look in the mirror and it just looks so obvious to me. So, I'm not completely convinced everyone sees it, but it still bothers me a lot.
